correctness.rationale: By source Theorem 1.7 the first Fourier zero k≈3.83171224396365 occurs in facet-normal directions. Compare P+tB with homothetic polygon Q_t=(1+t/r)P sharing offset facet support lines: the difference is 12 disjoint vertex caps, each area [tan(pi/12)-pi/12]t² and diameter O(t). Their Fourier effect is cap-area times sum of vertex cosines plus O(t³). The Fourier transform of Q_t scales exactly. A simple real root persists in this direction by implicit function theorem; derivative F′(k)<0. Since κ is infimum of all zero radii, the perturbed directional root is a valid one-sided upper bound. Steiner area expansion cancels the first-order root displacement, leaving η=-c*(sumcos/F′(k)-6k/pi)>0. Independent high-precision direct 12-edge divergence calculation gave k=3.8317122439636479540700049, F′=-0.65991482843667124, η=0.00014158574849173963225. Source mpmath interval checker separately brackets the sign; neither test alone proves the analytic remainder.

originality.rationale: The 2026 full primary Gómez-Serrano–Levitin–Platt–Polterovich article proves the dodecagon has maximal κ among regular even-sided polygons and fixes nearest-zero directions; the open unrestricted convex maximizer problem is not settled. Published Resultary affine-orbit theorem treats area-preserving linear images, not outer Minkowski addition by a disk. The present one-sided quadratic perturbation gives a distinct nonlinear local stability direction; best-of-knowledge novelty with specialist variational literature risk.

final_claim: For the area-pi regular dodecagon P, area-normalized outer parallel body K_t=sqrt(pi/Area(P+tB))*(P+tB) has nearest real Fourier zero satisfying κ(K_t)<=κ(P)-η t²+O(t³)<κ(P) for sufficiently small t>0, with 0.00014158574849<η<0.00014158574850. This is a one-direction upper bound, not the complete second derivative of the global nearest-zero functional.
